nodes.What it is: The basic rules of electricity a robot runs on: voltage, current, resistance (Ohm's law), power, and how to read a schematic. You use a multimeter and breadboard to check that a circuit does what you think before you plug in a motor.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Stable knowledge; free browser circuit simulators (Falstad, Wokwi) let students learn before buying parts.
nodes.Key players: Arduino, SparkFun, Adafruit (education); Texas Instruments app notes
nodes.Best resources: Arduino Learn hub; SparkFun & Adafruit tutorials; Falstad circuit simulator

nodes.What it is: A microcontroller (MCU) is a small computer on one chip that reads sensors and controls outputs such as motor-driver signals. Bare-metal firmware runs without an operating system; other MCU applications use an RTOS or an interpreter such as MicroPython.
nodes.Prerequisites: C programming; Electronics fundamentals for robots.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Available platforms include ESP32-S3 (dual-core 240 MHz, Wi-Fi/BLE and vector instructions), Raspberry Pi Pico 2 (RP2350), Teensy 4.1 (Cortex-M7 600 MHz) and STM32 devices. Arduino UNO Q pairs a Linux MPU with an STM32U585 MCU running Zephyr. Embassy provides an asynchronous embedded Rust framework.
nodes.Key players: Espressif, Raspberry Pi, STMicroelectronics, PJRC, Arduino, Rust Embedded WG
nodes.Best resources: Cornell ECE 4760 (RP2350, free lectures); PlatformIO; The Embedded Rust Book
nodes.Sources: https://www.espressif.com/en/products/socs/esp32-s3 ; https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/pico/pico-2-product-brief.pdf ; https://www.pjrc.com/store/teensy41.html ; https://docs.arduino.cc/hardware/uno-q/ ; https://ece4760.github.io/ ; https://platformio.org/ ; https://docs.rust-embedded.org/book/ ; https://embassy.dev/ ; https://www.raspberrypi.com/products/raspberry-pi-pico-2/

nodes.What it is: Buses are the ways chips and boards exchange data: UART is simple serial, I2C and SPI connect local peripherals, and CAN / CAN-FD support robust multi-node communication. A protocol, its physical wiring and the supported frame format must all match before devices can communicate.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: CiA describes Classical CAN, CAN-FD and CAN XL as three CAN generations. moteus uses CAN-FD; ODrive Pro/S1 support it with suitable firmware and configuration. ESP32-S3 TWAI supports Classical CAN only and requires an external transceiver; use an external CAN-FD controller plus a compatible transceiver for FD traffic.
nodes.Key players: CAN in Automation (CiA), Bosch, Espressif, SparkFun
nodes.Best resources: SparkFun I2C tutorial; CiA CAN knowledge pages; ESP-IDF TWAI docs

nodes.What it is: Smart servos such as Feetech STS and ROBOTIS DYNAMIXEL combine a motor, gearbox and controller. Compatible servos can share a daisy-chained serial bus and return feedback; SO-101 is one low-cost arm built this way.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: SO-101 uses six STS3215 servos per arm, including the gripper. The follower uses 1/345 gearing; the leader uses three 1/147, two 1/191 and one 1/345 servo. ROBOTIS documents DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 for compatible servo models.
nodes.Key players: Feetech, ROBOTIS, The Robot Studio, Hugging Face
nodes.Best resources: LeRobot SO-101 docs; Dynamixel Protocol 2.0 e-manual

nodes.What it is: A microcontroller pin can't power a motor; a motor driver (H-bridge, MOSFET stage) switches the battery current on and off very fast (PWM) to control speed and torque. This node covers brushed DC, stepper and the basics of brushless (BLDC) drivers, current sensing and heat.
nodes.Prerequisites: Electronics fundamentals for robots; Microcontrollers & bare-metal firmware.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Integrated driver ICs (e.g. TI DRV88xx) cover small robots; high-power robot joints use dedicated BLDC controllers.
nodes.Key players: Texas Instruments, Infineon, STMicroelectronics, ODrive Robotics
nodes.Best resources: TI DRV8833 datasheet and TI motor-driver app notes

nodes.What it is: Brushless motors are used in many legged robots and drones. Field-oriented control (FOC) uses motor angle and current information to control torque smoothly. Ready-made controllers and libraries let you learn FOC without first designing a power stage.
nodes.Prerequisites: Motor drivers & power electronics; basic control (PID).
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Katz's 2018 MIT thesis describes a low-cost modular actuator for dynamic robots. moteus and SimpleFOC publish open-source control code; current ODrive S1/Pro firmware is not publicly available, unlike the legacy ODrive repository. CubeMars and RobStride sell integrated actuators; protocol and ratings depend on the model.
nodes.Key players: ODrive Robotics, mjbots, SimpleFOC community, CubeMars, RobStride, MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab
nodes.Best resources: SimpleFOC docs; moteus reference manual; Katz MIT thesis 'A low cost modular actuator for dynamic robots'
nodes.Sources: https://simplefoc.com/ ; https://github.com/simplefoc/Arduino-FOC ; https://odriverobotics.com/ ; https://github.com/odriverobotics/ODrive ; https://github.com/mjbots/moteus ; https://github.com/mjbots/moteus/blob/main/docs/reference.md ; https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/118671 ; https://www.cubemars.com/ ; https://robstride.com/

nodes.What it is: Robots read the world through encoders, IMUs, current and force sensors. This node is the electrical side: ADCs, pull-ups, filtering noise, sampling rates and timestamps, so the data your AI model gets is clean.
nodes.Prerequisites: Microcontrollers & bare-metal firmware; Communication buses (UART, I2C, SPI, CAN).
nodes.Frontier state 2026: No specific 2026 change established. Current controller examples expose encoder and current feedback; sampling, filtering and timing remain application-dependent engineering tasks.
nodes.Key players: Adafruit and SparkFun (education and interfaces); Cornell ECE 4760 (signal processing labs); ODrive Robotics (controller feedback)
nodes.Best resources: Cornell ECE 4760 filtering, sampling and encoder examples; SparkFun I2C tutorial; ODrive controller documentation

nodes.What it is: A robot needs an energy source, suitable voltage regulation, protected wiring and a way to handle faults. Battery management systems monitor conditions such as cell voltage, temperature and current. Beginners should start with a current-limited bench supply or a protected commercial pack, not assemble loose lithium cells.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: No specific 2026 breakthrough established here. TI BQ76952 is an example of a 3-to-16-cell monitor/protector; Battery University explains how temperature, charge level and discharge depth affect lithium-battery life.
nodes.Best resources: Battery University BU-808 for cell care; TI BQ76952 product documentation for monitoring and protection concepts

nodes.What it is: Bigger robots pair the microcontroller with a small Linux computer (Raspberry Pi, Jetson, Arduino UNO Q) that runs cameras, ROS 2 and AI models, while the MCU handles hard real-time motor loops. Knowing how to split work between them is a key design skill.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Arduino UNO Q combines a Qualcomm QRB2210 running Debian with an STM32U585 running Zephyr. Raspberry Pi AI HAT+ offers Hailo-8L (13 TOPS) or Hailo-8 (26 TOPS) acceleration for Raspberry Pi 5; the host board and cooling are additional hardware.
nodes.Best resources: Arduino UNO Q docs; Raspberry Pi AI HAT+ product info; NVIDIA Jetson docs

nodes.What it is: Motor and balance controllers need predictable timing, for example a loop every 1 ms. An RTOS such as FreeRTOS or Zephyr, or real-time Linux with PREEMPT_RT, helps reduce scheduling delays but cannot by itself guarantee deadlines. You must measure jitter and validate worst-case execution, interrupt load and failure handling.
nodes.Prerequisites: Microcontrollers & bare-metal firmware; OS concepts (threads, interrupts).
nodes.Frontier state 2026: PREEMPT_RT was merged into mainline Linux 6.12 (Nov 2024) after ~20 years; Zephyr is used by Arduino UNO Q for its MCU side.
nodes.Key players: FreeRTOS (AWS), Zephyr Project (Linux Foundation), Linux kernel RT maintainers
nodes.Best resources: Lee & Seshia 'Introduction to Embedded Systems' (free, Berkeley EECS149); FreeRTOS and Zephyr docs

nodes.What it is: ros2_control connects ROS 2 controllers to hardware interfaces. micro-ROS provides a resource-constrained ROS 2 client on a microcontroller, typically communicating with an agent on a larger computer. Shared interfaces can support simulation and hardware, but drivers and timing still need testing.
nodes.Prerequisites: Embedded Linux & companion computers; ROS 2 basics.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: The rolling ros2_control documentation includes Embedded Integration and is a development-version reference. micro.ros.org redirects visitors to micro.vulcanexus.org; the ESP-IDF component supports ESP32-family boards. Select documentation matching the ROS distribution used by the lab.

nodes.What it is: EtherCAT is an industrial Ethernet fieldbus designed for short communication cycles and precise synchronization of devices such as motor drives. SOEM is a source-available EtherCAT master library usable from a suitable host; actual timing depends on the complete system.
nodes.Prerequisites: Communication buses (UART, I2C, SPI, CAN); Real-time OS & real-time control loops.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Originally developed by Beckhoff and specified in IEC 61158. ETG documents short cycle times and distributed-clock synchronization; these design capabilities are not guaranteed benchmark results for an arbitrary Linux setup.
nodes.Key players: Beckhoff, EtherCAT Technology Group, Open EtherCAT Society

nodes.What it is: Designing your own printed circuit board replaces a fragile nest of jumper wires with a clean, reliable board: schematic capture, layout, ordering from a fab. KiCad is the free, professional-grade tool.
nodes.Prerequisites: Electronics fundamentals for robots; Sensor interfacing & signal conditioning.

nodes.What it is: Running neural networks on the robot itself instead of the cloud: from tiny models on microcontrollers (TinyML) to vision accelerators (Hailo) to GPU modules (Jetson) that can run VLAs. Choosing the chip sets your latency, power and battery life.
nodes.Prerequisites: Embedded Linux & companion computers; deep learning basics.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: NVIDIA launched the Jetson AGX Thor developer kit in August 2025 from US$3,499; Jetson Thor specifications list up to 2070 FP4 TFLOPS, 128 GB and 40-130 W. Orin Nano Super is rated up to 67 TOPS; Hailo-8 up to 26 TOPS. Precision, model support and end-to-end latency differ, so these figures are not directly comparable. LiteRT for Microcontrollers and Edge Impulse support smaller MCU-scale models.
nodes.Key players: NVIDIA, Hailo, Google (LiteRT), Edge Impulse, Espressif
nodes.Best resources: NVIDIA Jetson pages; LiteRT for Microcontrollers guide; Edge Impulse docs

nodes.What it is: Simulators and emulators let you test firmware against virtual peripherals before connecting a physical circuit. Wokwi provides browser simulation and Renode emulates embedded systems. Hardware-in-the-loop is a separate setup using real hardware connected to a test environment; it is not automatically supplied by an emulator.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Renode is an open-source embedded-system simulation framework from Antmicro. Wokwi supports devices including ESP32, Arduino and Pi Pico, with browser access and separate paid integrations; check the chosen target and plan before using it in CI.

nodes.Node: Electrical safety & functional safety for robots
nodes.What it is: Safety engineering identifies hazards and designs a controlled response to faults, using measures such as guarding, limits, watchdogs and emergency stops. Simply cutting motor power can let a gravity-loaded arm fall, so the safe stopping method depends on the mechanism and risk assessment. A student prototype is not a certified safety system and needs competent review before public use.
nodes.Prerequisites: Motor drivers & power electronics; Batteries & power distribution.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: ISO 13849-1:2023 is edition 4 (April 2023), covering methodology for safety-related control-system design and integration. The public catalogue does not establish the safety functions or performance level needed for a particular robot; the full standard and application-specific requirements need specialist assessment.
nodes.Key players: ISO (standards publisher); competent machinery-safety engineers for application assessment
nodes.Best resources: ISO 13849-1:2023 public abstract; full standard for qualified design work (not replaced by a web summary)

nodes.Node: Open-source actuator & electronics stacks for legged/humanoid robots
nodes.What it is: Open robot designs show how actuators, power, wiring and embedded computers fit together. Berkeley Humanoid Lite uses BLDC actuators with 3D-printed gearboxes, while Open Duck Mini v2 uses a different, smart-servo-based stack. Reproducing either requires integration and safety work, not just downloading a policy.
nodes.Prerequisites: BLDC motor control & field-oriented control (FOC); Communication buses (UART, I2C, SPI, CAN); Batteries & power distribution.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Berkeley Humanoid Lite (2025) publishes hardware and software and reports hardware cost below US$5,000 using U.S. market prices. Open Duck Mini v2 publishes a roughly 42 cm biped and a target BOM below US$400. These are source-reported parts estimates, not delivered French lab budgets or guaranteed build outcomes.
nodes.Key players: UC Berkeley (Hybrid Robotics), Open Duck Mini community, MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab, mjbots
nodes.Best resources: Berkeley Humanoid Lite site/paper; Open Duck Mini repo

project_candidates.Description: Integrate a protected commercial battery pack and compatible BMS telemetry with a walking robot under experienced supervision. Do not assemble loose cells or treat a logging MCU as the pack protection system.
Knowledge nodes: Electrical safety & functional safety for robots
Open-source actuator & electronics stacks for legged/humanoid robots

project_candidates.Project: EtherCAT test cell with SOEM
project_candidates.Deliverable: Linux PC synchronously driving 2+ EtherCAT drives at 1 kHz, timing plotted.
project_candidates.Description: Learn industrial fieldbus for future partnerships with industrial robot makers.

project_candidates.Project: Reachy Mini custom expressive behaviours on the edge
project_candidates.Deliverable: Reachy Mini reacting to voice and faces with on-device models.
project_candidates.Description: Use Reachy Mini Wireless with onboard compute for appropriately small local models. The source lists US$499 before tax/shipping; Lite (US$399) requires an external computer. Benchmark model capacity and latency before promising a fully local voice pipeline.

project_candidates.Project: Experimental contact detection from servo telemetry
project_candidates.Deliverable: Controlled low-force bench experiment plotting servo telemetry against contact labels; compare a learned contact detector with a baseline and report failures.
project_candidates.Description: First verify the selected servo exposes usable current or load feedback and obtain contact labels with a reference sensor. If feedback is insufficient, report the negative result rather than infer force. This experimental detector must not replace independent stops or safety measures.
Knowledge nodes: Electrical safety & functional safety for robots

project_candidates.Project: Embedded Rust (Embassy) firmware for a robot joint
project_candidates.Deliverable: Rust async firmware closing a servo loop at 1 kHz, compared side-by-side with C version.
project_candidates.Description: Use an Embassy-supported RP2350 target and measure an async firmware control loop against a C baseline. The 1 kHz target is a benchmark goal, not an established end-to-end guarantee.

project_candidates.Project: Sim-matched digital twin of the arm electronics
project_candidates.Deliverable: Plots comparing a custom SO-101 servo/bus model against measured command-to-motion delay, saturation and deadband.
project_candidates.Description: Implement and validate servo/bus dynamics in a ROS 2 simulation interface. Renode can help with supported MCU firmware/peripherals but does not itself provide an SO-101 electromechanical twin.

project_candidates.Project: Joint bus shoot-out: serial vs CAN-FD vs EtherCAT
project_candidates.Deliverable: Plots comparing command/feedback latency and jitter for a DYNAMIXEL serial servo, a moteus CAN-FD endpoint and an EtherCAT drive.
project_candidates.Description: Use three protocol-compatible endpoints and a consistent host timing method. Report hardware, controller and load differences instead of attributing all performance differences to the bus.

project_candidates.Project: ros2_control driver for an EtherCAT servo drive
project_candidates.Deliverable: ROS 2 controller moving an industrial EtherCAT drive in sync with a simulated twin.
project_candidates.Description: Bridge SOEM and ros2_control so industrial drives can be used from the lab's ROS 2 stack.
